module purpose: neorv32_cpu_cp_crypto decodes supported crypto co-processor instruction fields from ctrl_i, latches rs1_i/rs2_i and function bits for accepted requests, computes XPERM, SHA-2, SM3, AES, and SM4 word transforms under the enabled generics, and returns the selected 32-bit result on res_o with valid_o when done.

use-case flows.value: accept a recognized crypto instruction, capture operands and function fields, and choose immediate completion or multicycle execution
compute the XPERM permutation result from rs1 and rs2
compute the SHA-2 or SM3 transform result from the captured operands and function bits
compute the AES or SM4 block-cipher transform result through byte selection, substitution, rotation, and final xor
signal completion of the current crypto result
write the selected result word to res_o when done is asserted
clear captured operands and qualifiers, completion state, result output, and AES/SM4 pipeline registers while rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.reasoning: Lines 274-293 decode enabled instruction encodings from ctrl_i fields into cmd, line 296 qualifies that decode with ctrl_i.alu_cp_alu to form cmd_valid, and lines 312-325 use cmd_valid to capture inputs and start execution. Integrity matters because a wrong accept/reject decision starts the wrong operation or suppresses a valid one; availability is established when an enabled encoding is present and ctrl_i.alu_cp_alu='1'. The flow graph leaves cmd and cmd_valid unreached, but the field records and RTL at lines 274-296 and 312-325 establish this control path.

conceptual assets.concept: Source operand values for the accepted crypto instruction
conceptual assets.reasoning: When cmd_valid='1', lines 313-314 capture rs1_i and rs2_i, and later computations consume those values in the XPERM path (lines 383, 389), SHA-2 path (lines 413-425), SM3 path (line 441), and block-cipher result path (line 475). Integrity matters because these formulas become incorrect if either operand is corrupted; availability is established only for accepted requests. The internal rs1 and rs2 registers are one-cycle copies used only by internal computations, so they are omitted as secondary pipeline storage under the section 6 restriction.

conceptual assets.concept: Captured operation qualifiers that select the crypto variant and result routing
conceptual assets.reasoning: Lines 315-316 copy ctrl_i.ir_funct3 and ctrl_i.ir_funct12 into funct3 and funct12 when cmd_valid='1'. Those stored fields later select the XPERM width (line 393), the SHA-2 formulas (lines 411-425), the SM3 formula (line 441), the block-cipher byte and rotation choices (lines 456-468), the AES mode (line 494), and the AES/SM4 variant behavior (lines 525, 560). Integrity matters because corrupted qualifiers choose the wrong computation or route the wrong result; availability is established while the captured fields are held between acceptance and result production.

Line 494 derives aes.dec from the enabled AES generics and funct12, line 500 uses it as the high lookup bit for aes_sbox_c, and lines 510-519 use it to select decrypt coefficients or the encrypt form for aes.mix1. Integrity matters because the wrong mode produces the wrong AES block-cipher transform. This decision exists only when EN_ZKNE or EN_ZKND is enabled; when both are disabled line 531 ties aes.dec low.

The control FSM stores S_IDLE, S_BUSY, and S_DONE in state and updates it at lines 325, 328, 333, and 337 after the case on line 320. This phase state decides whether a request completes immediately or takes the extra busy/done cycles, so integrity and availability of the implemented sequencing flow depend on these transitions.

done is cleared at line 319, asserted for immediate completion at line 327 and after the busy phase at line 336, gates result writeback at line 354, and is exported on valid_o at line 343. Integrity matters because corrupted status misreports result availability or suppresses result delivery; availability is established by the FSM paths at lines 320-337.

When EN_ZBKX is enabled, lines 383 and 389 compute xperm8_res and xperm4_res from the captured operands, line 393 selects xperm_res from those alternatives using funct3, and line 357 copies xperm_res to res_o when done='1' and out_sel="100". Integrity matters because the returned word must match the selected permutation; availability is established only under that done/selector condition. When EN_ZBKX is disabled, line 401 ties xperm_res low.

When EN_ZKNH is enabled, sha_core selects one of the SHA formulas from funct12 and computes sha_res from rs1 alone or from rs1 and rs2 (lines 411-425). In the readout path, line 364 copies sha_res to res_o when done='1', out_sel is not 100/101/110, and the SM3 selection at line 361 is false. Integrity matters because the returned word must match the selected SHA formula; availability is established only under those visible conditions. When EN_ZKNH is disabled, line 433 ties sha_res low.

When EN_ZKSH is enabled, line 441 computes sm3_res from rs1 using one of two rotate-xor forms selected by funct12(0). In the readout path, line 362 copies sm3_res to res_o when done='1' and line 361's SM3 condition is true. Integrity matters because the returned word must match the selected SM3 transform; availability is established only under those visible conditions. When EN_ZKSH is disabled, line 446 ties sm3_res low.

When any of EN_ZKNE, EN_ZKND, or EN_ZKSED is enabled, lines 456-460 select a byte from rs2, lines 463-472 choose and rotate the AES or SM4 intermediate word, and line 475 forms blk_res by xoring that rotated word with rs1. The AES path is implemented at lines 494-525 and the SM4 path at lines 544-565. Line 359 copies blk_res to res_o when done='1' and out_sel selects 101 or 110. Integrity matters because the returned word must match the selected AES/SM4 round transform; availability is established only under those visible conditions. When block-cipher features are disabled, line 484 ties blk_res low.
